answer: A bounded platform worker pool bounds only concurrent active work (the executing platform threads); an unlimited submission queue is outside that bound. It does not bound the number of admitted-but-waiting submissions or the queue depth, so the waiting backlog and its queueing delay can grow without limit. Because an unbounded queue never rejects, the pool can show few immediate errors while latency worsens; Little's Law (L = lambda x W) describes occupancy and response time growing once arrivals exceed completion rate. A deadline must therefore budget admission and executor queue wait, not only execution.
